decision.detail: I cap the pen, close the notepad, set it on the saucer by my coffee. I take the small Sony PCM-M1 recorder out of my coat pocket, press the red record button, hold it up so the crew can see the level meter twitch, then press stop. I tuck it back. I stand. I don't collect my bag. I walk to the coat rack, pull my wool coat off the hook, shake it once to hang it straight, put it on. I walk to the lobby door. I push it open. The February air hits me and I step out without looking back at the table.
decision.intention: Get to the Rialto before nine. Sit in the booth where Alma spent forty-two winters threading film. Record her one last time—her hands on the gate, her voice saying what she wants her daughter to know. One reel. The regional line takes it out tonight. Pittsburgh gets the voice. That is the piece. Not the party. Not the ballroom. Not the network's story. Mine.
decision.words: I'm taking the afternoon. Rialto closes at six. I want to be in that booth before the lights go out for good. Don't wait up.
